meta.title: Nowon Lee — Frontend Engineer
meta.description: Technical profile of frontend engineer Nowon Lee, focused on information accuracy, document generation progress, interface responsiveness, and service reliability

identity.name: Nowon Lee
identity.lead: I analyze when and why problems occur in web services and design solutions that fit the requirements and existing systems.
identity.supporting: When large API responses caused the screen to freeze, I moved JSON parsing and data transformation to a Web Worker. I designed how note updates are handled so that edits from each tab are preserved when the same note is edited in multiple tabs.

companies.summary: I developed the front end for the execution history detail view, server usage dashboard, and AI document generation service. I addressed freezes caused by large API responses and reduced the total data transferred by the server resource API. I designed a screen for reviewing drafts and generation details before download and discussed how to structure the API data needed to display them.

contributions.title: Reducing rendering delays in the execution history detail view
paragraphs: Users reported that the screen froze when they opened certain execution records. I identified affected records from one week of execution history and used Chrome DevTools’ Network and Performance panels to inspect API request and response processing times. For responses of 300 MB or more, converting the responses into display values took time.
I designed the execution history detail view so the Web Worker makes the API request, parses the JSON, and prepares the display values. The page receives only the converted values.
I set up a test environment to measure page performance before and after introducing the Web Worker. The displayed data stayed the same, and rendering delay fell from about 360 ms to 50 ms or less.

To reuse a worker across multiple APIs, I considered passing a page-defined conversion function through Comlink or generating modules for each API with code generation. The Comlink approach could run the conversion on the main thread, and per-API modules were unnecessary to resolve the freeze. I focused on fixing the affected page and left both approaches out.

contributions.title: Designing page modules around host routing and query caches
paragraphs: Our front end had to integrate as a library into a project that included another team’s service. The host team needed to control routing, and we could neither change its code nor provide a separate layout. I packaged the UI and behavior as page modules that the host could import without extra setup.

The pages shared the host’s QueryClient when available and used a shared QueryClient from the package otherwise. This kept cached values and cache reset rules consistent across pages for the same query key.

After deployment, I found that styles defined outside CSS layers could override the package styles inside Tailwind CSS layers. I changed the package to load Tailwind’s theme, base styles, and utilities without assigning them to layers.

contributions.title: Improving Docker image request intake and parallel execution
paragraphs: The message service could not consume the next Kafka request until the running task finished. We considered committing the Kafka offset immediately after receiving a message. Keeping pending requests only in memory could lose them on restart, so I designed the intake sequence to store the request and its status in the database before committing the offset.

The service retrieved pending tasks from the database and assigned one task to each available Pod from a pre-created pool. I addressed issues encountered when building the task engine as a Docker image so the Pods could be prepared in advance. Pending tasks remained available after a restart, and multiple Pods could run tasks concurrently.
In the existing execution history list, I designed the chart tabs and their selection state so users could view resource usage for each Pod.

contributions.title: Showing document drafts and generation details before download
paragraphs: User feedback showed that reviewing an AI-generated document required downloading it first. I evaluated a library for rendering HWPX files. Integrating it posed risks for the project, and it could not show document generation details.

To show the document content and generation details, I used the feedback to identify the necessary response fields, discussed them with the document generation API owner, and designed the screen and a Java proxy API.
Users could then view each section’s drafting status, the draft, and generation details before downloading.
The detail page link and download button became available as soon as the completion event arrived, even while the detail status API response was still pending.

contributions.title: Reducing document generation status requests
paragraphs: With periodic polling, short intervals made extra calls to the detail API even when the status had not changed. Long intervals could delay the progress shown on screen.

The existing SSE API sent events only when the generation stage changed. I designed the page to fetch details after each stage-change event and update the screen from the response. Detail API requests fell from 150–200 to 30 per document.

contributions.title: Reducing data transferred by the dashboard
paragraphs: I changed the dashboard to request only values newer than the previous request timestamp. Over 10 minutes, the amount of data transferred fell from 96.5 MB to 41 KB. I designed and implemented a Next.js API so the browser would no longer query Prometheus directly. I checked the values shown on the deployed dashboard against the API responses.

companies.summary: I made pages reflect user requests immediately, reduced the time it took for the first page to appear, and addressed issues that prevented real-time information from being shown. I documented the loading improvements so other projects could use the same approach.

contributions.title: Showing requested changes immediately and accurately
paragraphs: I made the page respond to user requests immediately, without waiting for a server response. I addressed mismatches between information on the page and server values, and reduced the request count by removing duplicate requests.

contributions.title: Shortening initial load and sharing a reusable setup
paragraphs: I reduced the time it took for pages to become visible to users. I documented the steps so other frontend projects could apply the same improvements.

contributions.title: Restoring real-time information updates
paragraphs: I used Chrome DevTools to find and fix intermittent WebSocket disconnections that stopped real-time information from updating.

contributions.summary: A URL could incorrectly match a route when it supplied an optional parameter without the preceding slash. I changed matching so patterns without a suffix could omit the optional parameter and its slash together. For patterns with a file extension, the parameter value can be omitted while the slash stays in place.
contributions.verification: I added tests for incorrectly matched URLs and existing file-extension patterns. The fix shipped in v7.13.1.

contributions.summary: Delete and Backspace could not remove the final character before an inline image in a regular paragraph or table cell. To preserve normal text and selection deletion, I applied a separate rule only when deleting a single remaining character immediately before an image with no text selected.
contributions.verification: The fix restored deletion of the final character before an image and shipped in v1.2.0.

items.title: AI Agent Workflow
paragraphs: I designed a wording review skill to help teammates understand AI-written documents at a glance. A script flags recurring informal phrases and wording whose meaning depends on context. The AI agent identifies what the passage refers to and what action it describes before revising it. For example, the skill can replace “document sharing boundaries” with an explanation of who can read a document under restricted sharing settings.

I designed a writing skill to help AI agents interpret user prompts correctly when drafting documents. The skill identifies the document’s purpose and the author’s intent, then applies a structure that fits. It can also tell the user what information the document still needs.

items.title: Personal Notes Workspace
paragraphs: I built a workspace for saving frequently used instructions and commands. Users can select content from several notes, arrange it, and copy it in one action.

To preserve edits from each tab without interrupting editing, I designed the data structure to merge insertions and deletions using Yjs’s Y.Text. To keep what each tab shows consistent with what is saved, the app saves to IndexedDB before notifying other tabs through BroadcastChannel. Those tabs read the saved changes. I designed an end-to-end test to check that edits from each tab appear.
I configured ESLint and JS Boundaries to allow imports between FSD layers only through designated entry points. I kept server and browser entry points separate so their modules would not be mixed.

I added arrow-key navigation to the batch-copy order menu using React Aria. Closing the menu returns focus to its trigger, and saving the order preserves focus in a note that is already being edited. I tested keyboard resizing and checked that bringing a note forward leaves the Tab order intact.

I placed the IndexedDB provider at the app root, the batch-copy provider in the layout shared by its screens, and the editor provider on each editing page. Autosave tests can inject only what they need, and implementations can change without editing UI code.

items.title: Offline Translation Web App
paragraphs: With language models saved ahead of time, users can translate between Korean and English or Korean and Japanese without a network connection and keep entering text on the page while the model runs.
I used browser caching and IndexedDB to store the files and information needed for translation, and automated deployment with GitHub Actions.
